follow-up time: Not specified, but mentioned as follow-up by a multidisciplinary team
exposure: CMS subtypes based on genetic mutations (CHAT, DOK-7, CHRNE)
cohort: 9 pregnant women with congenital myasthenic syndromes (CMS) followed at two tertiary hospitals
finding: Most pregnancies in women with CMS had no major complications for mothers or newborns, except for one case with a CHAT mutation who experienced symptom worsening during and after pregnancy.
